text: Most first-date conversations stall at "what do you do?" and "where are you from?" Both are fine icebreakers, and both tell you almost nothing. The five questions below dig a little deeper without turning the evening into an interview — they give the other person room to be interesting, and they give you something real to remember.

images.alt: Two coffee cups on a small table
images.caption: Slow conversations beat clever opening lines.

text: Curiosity is the most underrated form of flattery.
Try one of these the next time the conversation drifts toward small talk. You don't need all five — the point is to follow the thread of whichever one lights them up.

items: What's something you've changed your mind about in the last year?
What did you do last weekend that you actually enjoyed — not just attended?
Who in your life knows you best, and what would they say about you?
What's a small thing that's been bothering you this week?
What does a genuinely perfect Saturday look like for you?

text: Notice whether they ask you the same things back. The goal isn't to pass a test — it's to find out, in an hour over coffee, whether you're both curious about each other. If you are, the rest tends to take care of itself.
